2D convolution over an image feature map.

Slides filters x kernel x kernel windows over the [H, W, C] sample; the output has 'filters' channels and, with padding 'same' at stride 1, the same height and width (PyTorch Conv2d rules). Put an activation node after it. Runs on ArrayFire; the shapes on the As compiled card are the training shapes.

## Settings

| Group | Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Convolution | Output Channels | `filters` | Integer | `32` | `1-1048576` | The run | Number of output channels. Required. |
| Convolution | Kernel Size | `kernel_size` | Integer | `3` | `1-1048576` | The run | Square kernel width and height. Required. |
| Convolution | Stride | `stride` | Integer | `1` | `1-1048576` | The run | Spatial step between kernel applications. Required. |
| Convolution | Padding | `padding` | Choice | `same` | `same`, `valid` | The run | 'same' keeps the size at stride 1 (odd kernels); 'valid' adds none. Required. |
| Convolution | Bias | `use_bias` | On / off | `true` |   | The run | Adds a learned value per output channel. Turn it off when a BatchNorm follows (the BatchNorm's shift does the same job), as torchvision's ResNet and MobileNet do. |
| Fine-tuning | Frozen | `frozen` | On / off | `false` |   | The run | Keeps this layer's weights as they are while the rest of the model trains: no gradient step, no weight decay, no optimizer memory. Use it on layers that start from a weights file (fine-tuning), then turn it off to train them too. |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

## Usage

```text
Data Input (images) -> Resize -> Conv2D -> ReLU -> MaxPool2D -> Flatten -> Dense -> Output
```

```text
Input shape: (batch, channels, height, width). Output: (batch, out_channels, new_h, new_w).
```

## Tips

- 3x3 kernels are most common and efficient.
- Use stride=2 instead of pooling for modern architectures.
- Increase filters as you go deeper in the network.
